content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 9
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
19 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was, when-Solomon finished building ʾet-the-house-of YHWH and-ʾet-the-house-of the-king and-ʾet-all the-desire-of Solomon that he-desired to-do,

**LOGOS (formal):** As soon as Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the king's house and all that Solomon desired to build,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When Solomon had finished building the LORD's temple, the royal palace, and everything else he had wanted to build,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-you — if you-walk before-me as David your-father walked, in-integrity-of heart and-in-uprightness, to-do according-to-all that I-commanded-you, and-my-statutes and-my-judgments you-keep —

**LOGOS (formal):** And as for you, if you will walk before me, as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, doing according to all that I have commanded you, and keeping my statutes and my rules,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As for you — if you walk before me as your father David did, with integrity and uprightness, doing everything I have commanded and keeping my decrees and laws,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** If you-will-surely-turn — you and-your-sons — from-following-me, and-you-do-not keep my-commandments and-my-statutes that I-set before-you, and-you-go and-serve other gods and-bow-down to-them —

**LOGOS (formal):** But if you turn aside from following me, you or your children, and do not keep my commandments and my statutes that I have set before you, but go and serve other gods and worship them,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But if you or your descendants turn away from me, fail to keep my commands and decrees, and go off to serve and worship other gods,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-this house will-be a-heap-of-ruins. Everyone passing by-it will-be-appalled and-will-hiss, and-they-will-say, 'Why has YHWH done thus to-this land and-to-this house?'

**LOGOS (formal):** And this house will become a heap of ruins. Everyone passing by it will be astonished and will hiss, and they will say, 'Why has the LORD done thus to this land and to this house?'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And this temple will become a pile of rubble. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will whistle through their teeth, asking, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and this temple?'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-they-will-say, 'Because they-forsook ʾet-YHWH their-God, who brought-out ʾet-their-fathers from-the-land-of Egypt, and-they-seized other gods and-bowed-down to-them and-served-them — therefore YHWH brought upon-them ʾet-all this evil.'"

**LOGOS (formal):** Then they will say, 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt and laid hold on other gods and worshiped them and served them. Therefore the LORD has brought all this disaster on them.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt. They embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them. That is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-Hiram went-out from-Tyre to-see ʾet-the-cities that Solomon had-given to-him, and-they-were-not right in-his-eyes.

**LOGOS (formal):** But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, they did not please him.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But when Hiram traveled from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said, "What are-these cities that you-gave to-me, my-brother?" And-he-called-them the-land-of Cabul, to this day.

**LOGOS (formal):** Therefore he said, "What kind of cities are these that you have given me, my brother?" So they are called the land of Cabul to this day.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "What kind of towns are these you've given me, brother?" he said. He called the area Cabul — and the name has stuck to this day.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-this is the-account-of the-labor-levy that the-king Solomon raised to-build ʾet-the-house-of YHWH and-ʾet-his-own-house and-ʾet-the-Millo and-ʾet-the-wall-of Jerusalem and-ʾet-Hazor and-ʾet-Megiddo and-ʾet-Gezer.

**LOGOS (formal):** And this is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon drafted to build the house of the LORD and his own house and the Millo and the wall of Jerusalem and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer —

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Here is an account of the labor force King Solomon conscripted for his building projects — the LORD's temple, the royal palace, the Millo, Jerusalem's wall, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** Pharaoh king-of Egypt had-gone-up and-captured ʾet-Gezer and-burned-it with-fire, and-ʾet-the-Canaanites dwelling in-the-city he-killed. And-he-gave-it as-a-dowry to-his-daughter, the-wife-of Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and had given it as dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer, burned it down, killed its Canaanite inhabitants, and given the city to his daughter as a wedding gift when she married Solomon.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** and-ʾet-Baalath and-ʾet-Tamar in-the-wilderness, in-the-land,

**LOGOS (formal):** and Baalath and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Baalath, and Tadmor in the desert,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** and-ʾet-all the-storage-cities that Solomon had, and-ʾet-the-chariot-cities and-ʾet-the-cities-of the-horsemen, and-ʾet-the-desire-of Solomon that he-desired to-build in-Jerusalem and-in-the-Lebanon and-in-all the-land-of his-dominion.

**LOGOS (formal):** and all the store cities that Solomon had, and the cities for his chariots, and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** as well as all his storage cities, chariot cities, and cavalry cities — everything he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout his realm.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** All the-people who-were-left from-the-Amorites, the-Hittites, the-Perizzites, the-Hivites, and-the-Jebusites — who were not from-the-sons-of Israel —

**LOGOS (formal):** All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the people of Israel —

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The surviving non-Israelite populations — descendants of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites —

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 21
**EMET (literal):** their-sons who-were-left after-them in-the-land, whom the-sons-of Israel were-not able to-devote-to-destruction — Solomon raised from-them a-levy-of forced-labor, to this day.

**LOGOS (formal):** their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the people of Israel were unable to devote to destruction — these Solomon drafted to be slaves, and so they are to this day.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** those the Israelites had been unable to destroy completely, Solomon conscripted as forced laborers. They remain so to this day.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** But-from the-sons-of Israel Solomon did-not make a-slave, for they were the-men-of war and-his-servants and-his-officers and-his-captains and-the-commanders-of his-chariots and-his-horsemen.

**LOGOS (formal):** But of the people of Israel Solomon made no slaves. They were the soldiers, his servants, his commanders, his captains, his chariot commanders, and his horsemen.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon did not make slaves of any Israelites. Instead, they served as his soldiers, officials, commanders, captains, and chariot and cavalry officers.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** These were the-chiefs-of the-officers who were over the-work-of Solomon — five-hundred and-fifty, who-ruled over the-people who-did the-work.

**LOGOS (formal):** These were the chief officers who were over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty, who had charge of the people who carried on the work.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** There were five hundred and fifty chief officers supervising Solomon's labor force.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** Only the-daughter-of Pharaoh went-up from-the-City-of David to her-house that he-built for-her. Then he-built ʾet-the-Millo.

**LOGOS (formal):** But Pharaoh's daughter went up from the City of David to her own house that Solomon had built for her. Then he built the Millo.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he constructed the Millo.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon offered three times in-the-year burnt-offerings and-peace-offerings upon the-altar that he-built for-YHWH, and-he-burned-incense with-it — that which was before YHWH. And-he-finished the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** Three times a year Solomon used to offer up burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built to the LORD, making offerings with it before the LORD. So he finished the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built to the LORD, also burning incense before the LORD. So the temple was completed.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-Hiram sent in-the-fleet ʾet-his-servants, men-of ships, who-knew the-sea, with the-servants-of Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, seamen who were familiar with the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Hiram sent experienced sailors from his own fleet to serve with Solomon's men.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-they-came to-Ophir, and-they-took from-there gold — four-hundred and-twenty talents — and-brought-it to the-king Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** They went to Ophir and brought from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and they brought it to King Solomon.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** They sailed to Ophir and brought back 420 talents of gold for King Solomon.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
